input.quote: 11.6 Return of Confidential Information. Upon the effective date of the termination of this Agreement for any reason in its entirety, or with respect to a Product, either Party may request in writing and the non-requesting Party shall ... promptly destroy all copies of such Confidential Information in the possession or control of the non-requesting Party and confirm such destruction in writing to the requesting Party.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains a full exit/transition architecture, so no clause is missing. Section 11.6 gives a mutual, on-request return/destruction-with-written-certification mechanic for Confidential Information (with reasonable archival/back-up carve-outs), which is the data-return element the rule seeks and is not an immediate-deletion walk-away. Section 12.3 sets out detailed wind-down mechanics: transfer of Regulatory Approvals, Regulatory Materials, clinical and pharmacovigilance data within fixed periods (12.3(c)(iv), (d)(iii)), a defined Transition Assistance package including technical assistance and Know-How transfer for a stated post-termination period (12.3(c)(vi)C), inventory sell-off and transition services (12.3(c)(iii), (vi)G), and RevMed-side assistance to Sanofi on a Change of Control termination (12.3(e)); Section 7.2 obliges RevMed to transfer Manufacturing Know-How to Sanofi on request. Direction is structurally reversed from a typical hosting deal: because rights in the Products revert to RevMed on termination, most transition duties properly run from Sanofi to RevMed, so those obligations are the bargained reversion consideration rather than a rule breach and we do not flag them. Noted but not flagged: the durations are redacted ([***]) so we cannot confirm a 90-day/6-month floor, and Section 7.2 is not listed in the Section 12.4 survival list, so post-expiry manufacturing know-how support is not expressly preserved. Overall the clause set meets or exceeds the fallback position.
